faq.intro: In Helldivers 2, Super Earth fights one shared war against the Terminids, the Automatons and the Illuminate. You pick which front to drop into, and a game master at Arrowhead rotates the active campaigns and reshapes the war while you play. This companion reads the same numbers the game does.
points: Every planet has a health pool. Liberation campaigns run on a fixed 1,000,000; defense campaigns range from roughly 600,000 to over 2 million.
The pool refills on its own, usually 1.5% to 4.5% per hour, and the game master can raise that past 20% to stall a push. Defense campaigns run on a timer instead and never refill.
Each operation you complete takes health off the pool, so a planet falls in proportion to how many squads fight on it.

Some planets are split into regions such as towns and cities. While a region is being taken, the planet's own bar can stay at 0%, so the companion shows the region furthest along instead and names it.
The enemy pushes back too. Counterattacks land as sudden dips of 1 to 2% and often come in runs of three or four.
qa: Does abandoning an operation hurt liberation?
No. Only completed missions damage a planet's health pool, so dropping an operation costs you the rewards and nothing else.
Why do planets lose progress overnight?

Planets regenerate around the clock. Overnight, when fewer Helldivers are dropping, that regeneration outruns the damage players deal and you wake up to a lower percentage. Defenses work differently: they run on a fixed timer and never regenerate.
Do missions outside the campaign list count?

You can drop on any liberated planet, but those planets sit outside the active campaigns and regenerate faster than a handful of squads can damage them, so they stay at full health. The game master sees that traffic and can steer the war around it.
Where do the progress rates and estimates come from?

The API only reports the current state, with no history. Your browser keeps the snapshots it has seen for an hour and measures how fast each front moves, so rates and estimates appear about five minutes after you open the overview. Until then a front shows the enemy's regeneration, which is what Super Earth has to out-damage every hour.
Why do most fronts show no bar?
Most active campaigns sit at full enemy health at any given moment. Those fronts say “No ground taken yet” and sort below the ones that are moving.
